who: Sophocles · Women of Trachis, 5th century BC
quote: Your knowledge must come after you act. For you can have no test which is not fanciful except by making the attempt.
meaning: Thinking alone is just guessing. You only truly know by trying. Sophocles wrote this over 2,400 years ago.

quote: ...you could not confer such knowledge on anybody's intellect ... one's arms learnt (in an artist's way) to recognise what mattered. In my muscles I knew.
meaning: Years of lifting wood taught Sturt's arms what no lesson could. He ran his family's wagon-wheel shop from 1884.

who: Sri Ramakrishna · The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna, spoken 1884
quote: The almanac forecasts the rainfall of the year. But not a drop of water will you get by squeezing the almanac. No, not even one drop.
meaning: In 1884 he said a calendar can predict rain, but squeezing it gives no water. Only practice brings the real thing.

quote: There are some things in golf which cannot be explained in writing... They come to the golfer only through instinct and experience.
meaning: Vardon won the British Open six times, still the record. He said some golf skills only come from feel and doing.

who: John Keats · Letter to J. H. Reynolds, 1818
quote: Axioms in philosophy are not axioms until they are proved upon our pulses.
meaning: A wise idea is only true for you once you feel it in your body. Keats wrote this in 1818.

quote: You know that clever talk touching joinery will not make a chair; and I know that it is of about as much value in the physical sciences.
meaning: In an 1877 talk to workers, scientist Huxley said talking about chairs never built one, and science is the same.

who: Lu You · Reading on a Winter Night, 1199
quote: Knowledge gained from books alone is ultimately shallow; To grasp the essence of a matter, one must personally put it into practice.
meaning: What you learn from books stays thin. To truly know it, do it yourself. Lu You wrote this to his son in 1199.

who: William Harvey · On the Motion of the Heart and Blood, 1628
quote: I profess both to learn and to teach anatomy, not from books but from dissections; not from the positions of philosophers but from the fabric of nature.
meaning: In 1628 Harvey showed that blood moves in a circle. He learned by looking at real bodies, not by reading books.

quote: To define health and satiety, to penetrate their causes and conditions, is quite another thing from being well and satisfied.
meaning: Knowing about health is not the same as being healthy. Al-Ghazali left a top teaching job for 10 years to practise.

quote: ...one cannot teach by word, by the spoken explanation, alone... if my explanation fails to explain I take my violin and bow, and clear up the matter beyond any doubt.
meaning: Auer taught violinist Jascha Heifetz. In a 1919 book he said: when words fail, pick up the violin and show it.
